reviewContext.userProblem: Every flying-mail user-management operation (users/user queries, setUserRole, setUserActive, user mail and template permission rules, createUser, resendInvitation) requires a signed-in ADMIN web session via requireAdminUser. Every API key is refused, including the full-capability bootstrap key, so user administration cannot be done through the API or the flying-mail CLI. Realtime subscriptions cannot filter by event type.
requiredOutcomes: A USER_ADMIN API-key capability: domain enum, GraphQL enum, global classification and new migration 0017_user_admin_capability.sql widening the api_key_scopes CHECK. Existing migrations are not edited.

USER_ADMIN authorizes only users, user(id) (including rule listings), setUserRole, setUserActive, add/removeUserMailPermission and add/removeUserTemplatePermission. It never authorizes createUser or resendInvitation, and nothing else.

Only a signed-in ADMIN user session can grant USER_ADMIN (createApiKey and addApiKeyScope). API-key viewers, including KEY_ADMIN and KEY_ADMIN+USER_ADMIN keys, cannot grant it. The bootstrap key does not receive it.

Liveness: on every call, USER_ADMIN works only while the key is usable and its creator exists, is ACTIVE and has role ADMIN. Otherwise those operations are FORBIDDEN. The key's other capabilities are unaffected.
The last-active-admin invariant and no self-escalation hold through the API. Rules created through a key record the key's creator in createdByUserId.
Settings > API keys can grant USER_ADMIN, with a description and instance-wide scope rendering. Settings > Users keeps working.

CLI flying-mail user list/show/set-role/activate/deactivate/rule add|remove/template-rule add|remove, in the existing command style and with existing exit codes. FORBIDDEN exits 4 with a USER_ADMIN hint.

designDecisionsAndRationale: USER_ADMIN is a global capability that is inert by default. authorizesGlobal returns false for it for every viewer, so no scope-only check can accept it. Only requireUserAdministrator in auth-guards.ts accepts it, because liveness needs repository access (design 2.1, 2.3).

Guard order (design 2.3): USER viewer with role ADMIN; API key must hold the USER_ADMIN scope; key loaded and usable (deps.clock); non-null creator; creator exists, is ACTIVE and is ADMIN. The guard returns actorUserId = the creator id, which is used for audit createdByUserId. It runs before any read of the target user, so a refused key cannot probe ids.

Grant rule (design 2.5): the first branch of assertGrantable refuses USER_ADMIN for non-admin-session viewers. addApiKeyScope(USER_ADMIN) is allowed only for the admin who created the key (U1). The bootstrap key excludes USER_ADMIN.
Migration 0017 rebuilds api_key_scopes with the 0012 column definitions and USER_ADMIN appended to the CHECK. It has no PRAGMA statements and no backfill.

D15: MailEventScope.types is an optional field folded into matchesScope. lastSeq = row.seq stays outside the match branch. Filtering is per subscription in memory, never in SQL, so cursors stay global. A persisted state without types means all types.

CLI watch --type: short names map to enum values, are deduplicated and sorted in declaration order, and are parsed before any network call. The cursor key appends |types=<list> only when a filter is set.

CLI user commands use only existing GraphQL operations with variables, and resolve users by id or case-insensitive email. A FORBIDDEN error gets USER_ADMIN_HINT appended. CONFLICT and other errors pass through unchanged.
Plan DAG: wave 1 = 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06 (parallel, disjoint writePaths); wave 2 = 07 (depends on 01); wave 3 = 08 (serial reconciliation and final gates).
intentionalTradeoffs: U4: the last-active-admin read-then-write race also applies to USER_ADMIN key calls (accepted, design 7).
Viewer.capabilities lists USER_ADMIN for a dormant key. This is display only; authorization always goes through requireUserAdministrator.
A USER_ADMIN key's domainId:null scope makes visibleDomains return all domains, for CLI --domain resolution (U5 default).
Wave-1 plans may see transient test or typecheck failures in each other's files. Plan 08's full re-run is authoritative.
The user-admin-migration.test.ts cascade assertions rely on libsql.ts setting PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON asynchronously. If they are flaky, the plan 01 worker records it rather than editing libsql.ts.
supportedEdgeCases: Creator demoted, deactivated or deleted, or the key revoked after the viewer was resolved: the next USER_ADMIN call is FORBIDDEN, with a specific message.
Key with createdByUserId null: FORBIDDEN, no creating admin.
A key demotes its own creator: the call succeeds, the key's next call is FORBIDDEN, and it cannot restore the creator.
Creator is the only active admin: demote or deactivate through the key gives CONFLICT.
Unseeded keys holding USER_ADMIN (for example the schema-auth-hardening.test.ts root key) fail closed at the guard.
A USER_ADMIN key with an extra MAIL_READ scope keeps mail reads working regardless of creator liveness.

scope.types: empty list, LIVE or an unknown value gives BAD_USER_INPUT on scope.types. Duplicates collapse. types combines with domainId/address as AND. Two subscriptions on one connection with different types are independent.

watch --type: the order and repetition of values do not change the cursor key. --type= and --type live exit 2 with no network call. A legacy cursor entry without --type is still found by its literal key.
user rule remove with a rule id not owned by the target user exits 5, and no mutation is sent.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Web live-update type filtering (the web always subscribes to all types).
Pre-existing TEMPLATE_* global-capability drift in the web scope formatter.
